task: Escribe la respuesta completa de Eleanor a Daniel (120–150 palabras) o la continuación de la historia.
paragraphs: The letter arrived on a Tuesday, which was strange in itself, because nobody had written to Eleanor Hughes in years. Bills came, of course, and supermarket leaflets, but not envelopes addressed by hand in blue ink. She turned it over twice before opening it, as if the back might tell her something the front did not.

Inside was a single sheet of paper and an old photograph. The photograph showed a girl of about nineteen sitting on a sea wall, laughing at whoever was holding the camera. It took Eleanor a moment to recognise herself.

"Dear Ellie," the letter began. Nobody had called her Ellie since 1971. "You will probably be surprised to hear from me after so long. I found this photo while clearing out my late mother's house and I wanted you to have it. I have thought about that summer in Brighton more often than I should admit. I never explained why I didn't come to the station that day. The truth is that I was a coward. I was afraid of what my father would say, and by the time I found the courage, you had already gone to Canada. I am not writing to ask for anything. I simply wanted you to know that you were right to leave, and that I have never forgotten you. Daniel."

Eleanor sat down at the kitchen table. Outside, a neighbour was arguing with a delivery driver, and somewhere a radio was playing a song she half recognised. She read the letter again, more slowly this time, and noticed that there was an address at the top, a town only forty miles away.

For fifty years she had told the story of that summer as a joke: the boy who stood her up and changed the course of her life. She had built a career in Toronto, married, raised two children, buried her husband and come home. She had been, on the whole, happy.

She looked at the girl on the sea wall for a long time. Then she took a pen from the drawer, found a clean sheet of paper and, after a moment's hesitation, began to write: "Dear Daniel, you were late, but not too late for a cup of tea."
